templates.name: PostgreSQL
templates.description: A PostgreSQL server on this machine or your network, through psql.

templates.name: MySQL
templates.description: A MySQL server on this machine or your network, through the mysql client.

templates.name: MariaDB
templates.description: A MariaDB server, through the mariadb (or mysql) client.

templates.name: SQL Server
templates.description: Microsoft SQL Server through sqlcmd. Trusts the server's certificate, as local installs use a self-signed one.

templates.name: CockroachDB (insecure dev cluster)
templates.description: A cockroach start-single-node --insecure cluster. Uses the PostgreSQL protocol through psql.

templates.name: YugabyteDB (YSQL)
templates.description: YugabyteDB's PostgreSQL-compatible YSQL API on its default port.

templates.name: PostgreSQL in Docker
templates.description: Runs psql inside a postgres container with docker exec, so nothing needs to be installed locally and no port has to be published.
templates.help: Pick a running container. The user, database and password are read from the container's POSTGRES_* variables when it has them.

templates.name: MySQL or MariaDB in Docker
templates.description: Runs the mysql or mariadb client inside the container with docker exec.
templates.help: Pick a running container. Credentials come from its MYSQL_* or MARIADB_* variables when it has them.

templates.name: SQL Server in Docker
templates.description: Runs sqlcmd inside an mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server container.
templates.help: Pick a running container. The sa password is read from MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD when the container has it.

templates.name: SQLite database file
templates.description: Open an existing .db, .sqlite or .sqlite3 file, or create a new one.

templates.name: SQLite scratch database (in memory)
templates.description: An empty database that lives only while it is connected. Good for trying out SQL; everything is gone on disconnect.

templates.name: Supabase
templates.description: Supabase's PostgreSQL database, directly or through its connection pooler.
templates.help: In Supabase open Project Settings → Database (or Connect) and copy the connection string into Connection URL. The pooler hosts look like aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com.

templates.name: Neon
templates.description: Serverless PostgreSQL from Neon.
templates.help: In the Neon console open Connect, choose psql and copy the connection string into Connection URL.

templates.name: Amazon RDS / Aurora PostgreSQL
templates.description: PostgreSQL on Amazon RDS or Aurora.
templates.help: Use the instance's endpoint from the RDS console (Connectivity & security). The instance must accept connections from your address.

templates.name: Amazon RDS / Aurora MySQL
templates.description: MySQL or MariaDB on Amazon RDS or Aurora.
templates.help: Use the instance's endpoint from the RDS console (Connectivity & security).

templates.name: Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
templates.description: Cloud SQL through the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy running on this machine.
templates.help: Start the proxy first, for example: cloud-sql-proxy <project>:<region>:<instance> --port 5432. Lightpad then connects to 127.0.0.1.

templates.name: Google Cloud SQL for MySQL
templates.description: Cloud SQL through the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy running on this machine.
templates.help: Start the proxy first, for example: cloud-sql-proxy <project>:<region>:<instance> --port 3306.

templates.name: Azure Database for PostgreSQL
templates.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server.
templates.help: Copy the server name and admin user from the server's Overview page in the Azure portal.

templates.name: Azure SQL Database
templates.description: Azure SQL Database with SQL authentication. The server certificate is verified.
templates.help: Copy the server name from the database's Overview page. The server firewall must allow your address.

templates.name: PlanetScale
templates.description: PlanetScale's MySQL-compatible database. Requires TLS with a verified certificate.
templates.help: In PlanetScale click Connect, create a password, choose "General" and paste the connection string into Connection URL.

templates.name: DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL
templates.description: A DigitalOcean managed PostgreSQL cluster.
templates.help: Copy the connection string from the cluster's Connection details panel.

templates.name: DigitalOcean Managed MySQL
templates.description: A DigitalOcean managed MySQL cluster.
templates.help: Copy the connection details from the cluster's Connection details panel.

templates.name: Heroku Postgres
templates.description: Heroku Postgres. Heroku rotates the credentials, so paste a fresh URL when they change.
templates.help: Run heroku config:get DATABASE_URL -a <app> and paste the result into Connection URL.

templates.name: Render PostgreSQL
templates.description: A Render PostgreSQL instance through its external URL.
templates.help: Copy the External Database URL from the database's Info page and paste it into Connection URL.

templates.name: Railway (PostgreSQL or MySQL)
templates.description: A Railway database through its public TCP proxy.
templates.help: Copy the public connection URL (DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL or MYSQL_PUBLIC_URL) from the service's Variables tab and paste it into Connection URL; the type changes to match.

templates.name: CockroachDB Cloud
templates.description: CockroachDB Cloud through the PostgreSQL protocol, with a verified certificate.
templates.help: Click Connect on the cluster, choose General connection string and paste it into Connection URL.

templates.name: Timescale Cloud
templates.description: A Timescale Cloud service (PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB).
templates.help: Copy the service URL from the service's overview and paste it into Connection URL.

templates.name: TiDB Cloud
templates.description: TiDB Cloud Serverless through its MySQL-compatible endpoint, with a verified certificate.
templates.help: Click Connect on the cluster, choose General and copy the host, port and user (the user has a prefix like 4xyz.root).
